title: Network change observability checklist and fast rollback proto
body:
Summary

This is a lightweight PRD draft for a 'rollback-first' observability checklist and prototype telemetry envelope for customer-managed networking changes in Private deployments. The goal: make approval gates and audit logs not just about evidence accumulation but about enabling rapid, safe rollbacks when changes degrade customer SLAs.

Why this is different

Most existing proposals focus on exhaustive attestation and long-term retention. This doc proposes a compact, delta-driven telemetry envelope whose primary consumer is the automated rollback decision path. We assume customers prefer shorter proof bundles for routine, higher-frequency changes and full proofs for high-risk events.

Goals

- Provide a minimal telemetry contract that captures the signals necessary for automatic and manual rollback decisions while still satisfying base auditability.
- Design approval gate metadata fields that encode rollback-safe heuristics (e.g., expected impact window, safe-state snapshot id, observable canary metrics).
- Define a runbook and checklist for operators and customers to exercise fast rollback (<= 3 minutes tooling path) with clear audit trail linking the rollback to the approval tokens.

Non-goals

- This draft does not prescribe retention durations for full forensic archives (that is a separate retention/norms PRD).
- Not proposing major infra changes to customer-side logging collectors; we expect to work on compact adapters.

Success metrics (initial)
- Time-to-rollback (measured from anomaly detection to rollback enactment) <= 3 minutes in 90% of rehearsals.
- Percent of rollbacks with complete minimal telemetry envelope attached >= 95%.
- Reduction in mean time to resolution (MTTR) for network-induced customer incidents by 35% in pilot teams.

User stories
- Platform operator: "When a canary fails after a VPC ACL update, I want an automated rollback path that uses the approval token and snapshot id so I can revert with a single confirmed command and have the change auditable."
- Customer security lead: "I need to see exactly which approval gate accepted the change, the canary results, and the compact proof bundle so I can validate the incident postmortem without pulling terabytes of logs."
- SRE on customer side: "I want a CLI that references a compact evidence id and triggers the rollback path which includes toggling routing and re-applying the safe-state snapshot."

Proposed solution (high level)

1) Compact telemetry envelope (Delta-Proof)
- Purpose: capture the minimum fields needed to (a) understand the change, (b) validate that the change passed the stated canary checks, and (c) provide signatures/anchors to the approval gate.
- Required fields (minimal): change_id, approval_token_id, actor, change_digest (hash), safe_snapshot_id, canary_metrics_summary (key/value pairs, e.g., latency_pct_95_delta:+12%), timestamp, signed_by (operator/cust key id), short_retention_hint (enum: day/7d/30d).
- Optional fields: full_log_ref (S3/forwarding id), topology_hash, rollback_playbook_ref.
- Compression principle: store only deltas for topology and kv-caches; full logs are referenced by id not inlined.

2) Approval gate metadata enhancements
- Add 'rollback_mode' to gate config: {immediate-auto, manual-review, staged-canary}.
- Add 'expected_impact_window' (ISO duration) and 'safety_snapshot_policy' (auto-snapshot: before-change | customer-snapshot-required).
- Approval tokens must link to safe_snapshot_id or explicitly mark 'no-snapshot' with elevated review.

3) Fast rollback path (operator flow)
- Detection -> Decision: observability triggers (canary fail or metric breach).
- If approval_token.rollback_mode == immediate-auto and canary_metrics_summary breaches threshold, system posts rollback task referencing change_id and safe_snapshot_id.
- Manual-confirm path: operator CLI shows compact envelope summary and requires single confirmation to begin automated revert steps (reapply snapshot + route update).
- Audit attach: rollback action creates a rollback_receipt (fields: rollback_id, initiator, reason, linked_change_id, pre_revert_checksum, post_revert_checksum). The rollback_receipt is signed and stored alongside the original envelope.

4) Customer-managed networking integration notes
- We cannot mandate customers’ snapshot tooling; provide SDK adapters: (a) snapshot-stub API for common cloud providers (AWS, GCP, AZ) and (b) 'lightweight-acceptance' hook so customers can opt into automated snapshot creation on change.
- Design the envelope to work even when only a topology hash is available: operator must be able to verify pre/post hashes if full snapshots unavailable.

Data retention and privacy
- The compact envelope contains minimal PII; operator identity is recorded as key ids not raw credentials.
- Retention hints: default envelope retention = 7 days, allow customer override; full logs remain under customer control (referenced by id).

Rollout plan (pilot)
- Phase 0 (2 weeks): internal prototype with SRE and infra teams; implement envelope schema and CLI tooling to attach rollback_receipts.
- Phase 1 (4 weeks): pilot with 2 customers on Private deployments who opt into 'rollback-first' mode; gather rehearsals and measure TTR.
- Phase 2 (ongoing): maturity: add richer canary schemas, UI in Console for rollback decisions, and opt-in audit archival.

Operational checklist (for runbook authors)
- Pre-change: ensure safe_snapshot_id exists or policy set to require snapshot.
- During change: capture compact envelope; run lightweight canary suite; attach canary metrics summary.
- Post-change: schedule automated verification (5–15 min); if breaches, trigger rollback path and tag incident.
- Post-rollback: generate rollback_receipt and attach to change's proof bundle; run incident postmortem.

Open questions / risks
- Compliance: will compact envelopes satisfy all auditors for regulated customers? If not, we must provide forced full-proof retainment mode.
- Customer tool variety: some customers will not support snapshots — we must be explicit about degraded guarantees in that case.
- Approval token expiry windows and replay risk: need token revocation and TTL model.

Next steps
- Evan: prototype envelope schema and sample serializer + verification CLI (2 weeks).
- Marco: implement approval_token.rollback_mode in the approval service and wire token->snapshot linking (3 weeks).
- Leah: draft Console UI wireframe showing compact envelope and one-click rollback flow (2 weeks).
- Schedule pilot outreach: ops-eng + 2 customers; draft pilot success runbook (owner: Aisha).

Appendix: example compact envelope (one-line JSON example)
- {\"change_id\":\"chg-20250902-91a\",\"approval_token_id\":\"tok-331\",\"actor\":\"ops:marco\",\"change_digest\":\"sha256:...\",\"safe_snapshot_id\":\"snap-20250902-3\",\"canary_metrics_summary\":\"latency_p95:+12%\",\"timestamp\":\"2025-09-02T18:12:03Z\",\"signed_by\":\"key:evan-l\",\"short_retention_hint\":\"7d\"} 

Notes

This is intentionally lightweight and focuses on enabling the rollback path. Feedback wanted on the envelope field choices (esp. canary_metrics_summary schema) and approval token lifecycle constraints.
